summary: --full's dependent-sync resumability (internal/cli/sync.go: planDependentSync, runDependentFanOut) is a two-tier design: a sweep cursor (sync_state key "<resource>:full_progress") that advances UNCONDITIONALLY by however many RAW POSITIONS of the sweep window a batch consumed (not a count of ids selected -- a position whose id is already in the backlog is still "passed" even though it isn't separately fetched, and counting selections instead of positions systematically under-advances whenever a backlog id sits inside the window, which is always true right after a pass wraps), plus a separately persisted failed-id backlog (sync_state key "<resource>:full_failed", a comma-joined id list) that gets retry priority on subsequent calls. Capping under --max-parents reserves at least half the cap (rounding up) for the sweep, with unused budget hand-backable in EITHER direction (backlog->sweep when the backlog is smaller than its reservation; sweep->backlog when the sweep runs out of fresh ids before filling its reservation, including the degenerate case where the entire window is backlog-shadowed). At exactly --max-parents 1 that reservation formula gives the sweep the only slot on every call, which would starve the backlog forever -- a third persisted bit (sync_state key "<resource>:full_turn", 0/1, flipped unconditionally every call via SaveSyncStates) alternates which tier gets that single slot, so over any two consecutive calls both tiers get a turn whenever both have pending work. All three sync_state rows are written together via SaveSyncStates (internal/store/store.go, a variadic atomic-transaction primitive), never as separate SaveSyncState calls -- a crash or a single write failure between them can never leave the checkpoints out of sync with each other. Any future dependent that adds --full offset tracking must use this same shape (unconditional positional sweep advancement + separate backlog + bidirectionally-rebalanced reserved budget + turn-based tiebreak at cap 1 + atomic multi-row persistence) -- five different narrower variants were each found broken by review before landing here (see reason).
reason: Found across five consecutive rounds of review on the upstream PR splitting this branch's work (mvanhorn/printing-press-library#1773 and #1774) -- four from Greptile's automated review, a fifth from an independent blind code-review pass requested explicitly because four straight Greptile-only rounds risked over-fitting to what one automated checker happened to flag. Round 1: the original implementation advanced the durable offset for every planned id before a single network/store operation ran, so ANY failure anywhere in a batch left the offset advanced past ids never actually fetched. Round 2 (gate advancement on zero failures in the whole batch): a parent that fails CONSISTENTLY would then permanently pin the sweep at the start of its own window. Round 2.5 (advance past the leading run of successes): a chronically-failing id that sorts FIRST in its window still pinned the sweep at that exact position forever. Round 3 prompted the two-tier redesign (unconditional sweep + separate backlog). Round 4 then found two problems in THAT redesign: backlog-first ordering with no reserved sweep budget let a large backlog consume the whole cap every call; and the two sync_state rows were written via separate calls that could diverge on a crash or partial write -- fixed with a reserved-budget split and an atomic pair-write. Round 5 (the blind review) found the round-4 fix was STILL broken in three ways the four Greptile rounds never surfaced, because it needed multi-call state-machine reasoning rather than single-diff inspection: (a) at --max-parents 1 specifically, the reservation formula gives the sweep 100% of every call, and once the backlog also grows to cover the entire current window (dedupedSwept empty), plan.ids came out completely EMPTY despite real pending work -- runDependentFanOut's empty-plan short-circuit then silently reported "already_up_to_date", masking a permanent deadlock; (b) that same cap-1 case permanently starved the backlog even when NOT empty, violating the documented "retried on the very next call" guarantee; (c) fullSweepCount was computed by counting SELECTED sweep ids, not raw window POSITIONS consumed, so the cursor systematically under-advanced whenever a backlog id overlapped the sweep window (guaranteed after any wrap), causing indefinite oscillation/duplicate refetching rather than data loss. Fixed with: a positional walk that tracks positions-consumed independent of selection count; bidirectional budget hand-back between the two tiers; and a persisted turn bit that alternates exclusive priority specifically at cap 1. A separately-run automated code-review pass independently rediscovered the same position-vs-count bug (finding (c)) via static analysis alone, corroborating it from a second angle.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test and verify_skill.py all green (govulncheck not run locally, no dependency changes); go test -race scoped to every dependent-fan-out test confirms the failedIDs/backlog/turn bookkeeping introduces no data race. Nine end-to-end regression tests drive the real fetch/store path (not planDependentSync in isolation, which can't observe fetch failures), each pinned to a specific round's finding: TestFullSyncOffsetDoesNotAdvancePastAPartialBatchFailure (round 1). TestFullSyncOffsetSweepNeverWedgesOnAChronicallyFailingFirstID (round 3). TestFullSyncOffsetFailedIDGetsBacklogPriorityAcrossCalls (round 3 backlog half). TestFullSyncOffsetLargeBacklogDoesNotStarveSweep (round 4a). TestFullSyncOffsetMaxParentsOneNeverEmptiesPlanWithPendingWork (round 5a -- 12 consecutive --max-parents 1 calls with both ids always failing; asserts plan.ids is never empty while totalPending>0). TestFullSyncOffsetMaxParentsOneAlternatesBothIDsGetRetried (round 5b -- same setup, asserts both ids are actually attempted at least once across 12 calls via a call-counting fake client). TestFullSyncOffsetWrapWithOverlappingBacklogAdvancesPastWholeWindow (round 5c -- seeds a wrapped-pass state where the entire sweep window is already in the backlog, asserts the cursor still advances rather than stalling at 0). TestSaveSyncStates_WritesAllRowsTogether (store package -- confirms all three sync_state rows land with the values passed in one call). TestPlanDependentSync_FullResumesAcrossCallsAndWrapsAfterACompletePass and TestPlanDependentSync_DryRunDoesNotPersistFullOffset (pre-existing coverage) updated for the new shape via the commitFullOffset test helper. Round-14 live-account verification (7 consecutive --full workout_details calls, --max-parents 40 x5 then 2 x2, ~3,596 workouts) confirmed guarantee (1) -- the sweep cursor advanced monotonically by exactly --max-parents every call, cross-checked against a direct COUNT(*) of newly-synced rows with zero divergence at any checkpoint. Guarantee (2) (failed-id backlog retry) was NOT exercised live -- zero fetch failures occurred naturally across all 204 requests, so the backlog/turn starvation path was never triggered; it remains verified only by the unit tests above. The same round also flagged the turn bit appearing to flip once then stay flat for several calls, which looked inconsistent with "flips unconditionally every call" -- added TestFullSyncTurnBitFlipsEveryCallAcrossMixedCapSizes, which drives the identical 7-call sequence (500 synthetic ids, all succeeding) through the real fetch/store path and asserts the turn bit alternates 1,0,1,0,1,0,1; it reproduces the round's exact offset progression (40,80,120,160,200,202,204) but the turn bit DOES flip correctly every call in this reproduction, so the live discrepancy is most likely an artifact of how that round's raw-SQL observation tool read the database rather than a code defect -- flagged back to the live-testing session for confirmation, not silently dismissed. Also confirmed: last_synced_at updates on all three sync_state rows on every call (a single timestamp is used for the whole atomic transaction in SaveSyncStates, regardless of which rows' content actually changed) -- intended, not a bug; it cannot be used to infer when a row's content last changed, only when it was last written.
